Thank you. Thank you, Chairman, members. Last year I brought a bill before this ORG to clamp down on the rampant fraud which plagues our worker's compensation system. The bill was signed into law and as pf February this has already resulted in the prevention of more than 8,000 fraudulent claims, totaling nearly $60 million. ORG is a follow up on that effort. The bill targets a fraudulent business model that is growing in popularity where crooked doctors and attorneys partner up to take advantage of blue-collar, often immigrant, workers. The scam goes like this. The workers receive a cold call from someone offering to inform them of their healthcare rights. During that conversation, the caller fishes for information with the goal of signing the worker up for a cumulative trauma claim. Before they know it the worker has a lawyer that they haven't met, multiple Doctor's appointments, and a trauma claim filed on his or her behalf. All regardless of the worker's actual medical condition. Once tens of thousands of dollars in Doctor's bills have been rung up and filed as a medical lien, the attorney uses the lien as leverage to entice the employer or the insurance company into settling the case for nuisance value. Known as a compromise and release, the settlement also relieves the employer of any responsibility for future medical care for the employee. Again, regardless of the worker's actual medical condition. After the settlement is accepted, the Doctor accepts payment on the lien of just cents on the dollar. The Doctor and the attorney walk away with thousands of dollars in their pocket and move on to the next worker to run the scam again. AB 221 disrupts this model by pitting the Doctor against the attorney. The bill is set up to create an either or situation. Either the medical treatment is determined to be compensable by the employer, or a qualified medical examiner, or the appeals port. Or the case cannot be settled for a nuisance value of under 25 grand. If neither of these conditions are met, then the employer has no liability to pay the medical lien. Without the ability to use the medical lien as a hammer to leverage settlement, the fraudulent partnership between the doctors and the attorneys falls apart. Throughout the conversation with stakeholders, it has been acknowledged that this scam is happening. We know it is costing the workers compensation system tens of millions of dollars every year and leaving fewer resources behind for legitimate claims. The concern from stakeholders is largely about unintended consequences. I have repeatedly asked for specific examples of legitimate cases which would be unable to fulfill one of the requirements listed in the bill. Either demonstrating that the medical treatment is compensable or settle for a legitimate case over $25,000 and not a nuisance settlement. While many hypotheticals have been offered to me, not one concrete example that we can point to. This is the first policy Committee in the first house and sometimes it takes a while to concretely identify problems or loopholes, I understand that. And if problems are identified, I am committed to working with stakeholders to ensure that this bill successfully clamps down on this scam without infringing on legitimate worker rights. Every day we fail to take action, more workers are taken advantage of, fewer resources are available to the workers who really need the care. With me today, NONLEGISLATOR is a expert on the policy. I'm going to have him walk us through maybe a specific example of a fraudulent claim. And then certainly be available to the ORG to answer any questions the members may have.
Go ahead Mr Silver.
